Casablanca-Morocco.name: Casablanca
Casablanca-Morocco.evidence_basis: Tiny Chaouia anchorage (~1.5k in 1830, Miège trade archives), ~25k at 1907 French landing, transformed into Morocco's industrial metropolis in Protectorate/RGPH censuses (1926: 106,608; 1936: 257,430; 1952: 682,388; 1960: 965,277; 1971: 1,506,373).

Algiers-Algeria.name: Algiers
Algiers-Algeria.evidence_basis: 1830 French expeditionary survey (~30k intra-muros), Recensements Generaux de l'Algerie (1856-1954 municipal proper; 1954 Greater Algiers metro ~587k), and 1966 ONS census capturing post-1962 European exodus and rapid Algerian rural-to-urban influx.

Tripoli-Libya.name: Tripoli
Tripoli-Libya.evidence_basis: Karamanli/Ottoman capital (~25k in 1830; 1911 urban+Menscia oasis ~73k), ISTAT Censimenti della Libia (1931: 71,714; 1936: 98,861), and Libyan UN/national censuses (1954: 129,728; 1964: 213,506; 1973 oil-boom metro: 551,477).

Tunis-Tunisia.name: Tunis
Tunis-Tunisia.evidence_basis: Husaynid capital (~100k in 1830, ~125k at 1881 French Protectorate), Denombrements de la Tunisie (1921: 171,672; 1936: 219,578; 1946: 364,593), and INS censuses (1956-1975 municipal proper).

Oran-Algeria.name: Oran
Oran-Algeria.evidence_basis: 1831 French garrison count (~10k after 1790 earthquake recovery), Recensements Generaux de l'Algerie (1856-1954, European majority through 1954), and 1966 ONS census showing temporary slowdown after 1962 pied-noir departure.

Rabat-Morocco.name: Rabat
Rabat-Morocco.evidence_basis: Atlantic port (~25k in 1830) chosen by Lyautey as French Protectorate capital (1912); Recensements du Maroc (1926: 38,044; 1936: 83,379; 1952: 156,209) and RGPH (1960: 227,445; 1971: 367,620).

Constantine-Algeria.name: Constantine
Constantine-Algeria.evidence_basis: 1837 French conquest estimate (~25k), Recensements Generaux de l'Algerie (1856-1954, consistently Muslim-majority inland capital of Eastern Algeria), and 1966 ONS census.

Marrakech-Morocco.name: Marrakech
Marrakech-Morocco.evidence_basis: Southern imperial capital (~50k in 1830; Deverdun historical estimates), Recensements du Maroc (1926: 149,263; 1936: 190,314; 1952: 215,312), and RGPH censuses (1960: 243,134; 1971: 332,741).

Fez-Morocco.name: Fez
Fez-Morocco.evidence_basis: Largest pre-colonial Moroccan imperial capital (~85k in 1830, Le Tourneau), eclipsed after capital moved to Rabat (1912); Recensements du Maroc (1926: 81,172; 1936: 144,424; 1952: 179,372) and RGPH (1960: 216,133; 1971: 325,327).

Benghazi-Libya.name: Benghazi
Benghazi-Libya.evidence_basis: Cyrenaican capital (~8k in 1830, ~35k at 1911 Italian landing, stagnant to 1931 during Sanusi pacification war), ISTAT censuses (1931: 34,252; 1936: 48,510), and Libyan censuses (1954: 69,718; 1964: 137,295; 1973: 266,196).

Meknes-Morocco.name: Meknes
Meknes-Morocco.evidence_basis: Alawite imperial city (~30k in 1830) expanded as French agricultural and military hub; Recensements du Maroc (1926: 29,930; 1936: 74,702; 1952: 140,380) and RGPH (1960: 175,943; 1971: 248,369).

Annaba-Algeria.name: Annaba
Annaba-Algeria.evidence_basis: 1832 French occupation estimate (~6k), Recensements Generaux de l'Algerie (1856-1954, major iron-ore and phosphate export port), and 1966 ONS census.

Tangier-Morocco.name: Tangier
Tangier-Morocco.evidence_basis: Diplomatic seat (~10k in 1830, Miège) and International Zone (1923-1956) experiencing WWII/postwar boom; International Zone estimates and RGPH censuses (1960: 141,714; 1971: 187,894).

Oujda-Morocco.name: Oujda
Oujda-Morocco.evidence_basis: Eastern frontier oasis occupied 1907 and expanded as rail/mining gateway to Algeria; Recensements du Maroc (1926: 19,976; 1936: 34,523; 1952: 80,546) and RGPH (1960: 128,645; 1971: 175,532).

Sfax-Tunisia.name: Sfax
Sfax-Tunisia.evidence_basis: Olive-oil and Gafsa phosphate export port (~15k in 1830, bombarded 1881); Denombrements de la Tunisie (1921: 27,723; 1936: 43,333; 1946: 54,637) and INS censuses (1956: 65,635; 1975: 171,297).

Sale-Morocco.name: Sale
Sale-Morocco.evidence_basis: Historic twin medina across the Bou Regreg from Rabat (Brown monograph); Recensements du Maroc (1926: 20,965; 1936: 31,823; 1952: 46,582) and RGPH (1960: 75,799; 1971: 155,557).

Kenitra-Morocco.name: Kenitra
Kenitra-Morocco.evidence_basis: Founded 1912 by Resident-General Lyautey as Sebou river port serving the Gharb plain; Recensements du Maroc (1926: 9,931; 1936: 17,601; 1952: 55,905) and RGPH (1960: 86,775; 1971: 139,206).

Setif-Algeria.name: Setif
Setif-Algeria.evidence_basis: Small pre-colonial garrison town revived after 1838 French occupation and 1853 Compagnie Genevoise concession; Recensements Generaux de l'Algerie (1856-1954) and 1966 ONS census (98,504).

Tetouan-Morocco.name: Tetouan
Tetouan-Morocco.evidence_basis: Andalusian medina (~20k in 1830, briefly occupied by Spain 1860) made capital of Spanish Morocco (1913); Spanish Protectorate censuses (1936: 49,535; 1950: 80,732) and RGPH (1960: 101,352; 1971: 139,105).

Blida-Algeria.name: Blida
Blida-Algeria.evidence_basis: 1830 Mitidja oasis town estimate (~9k, recovering from 1825 earthquake), Recensements Generaux de l'Algerie (1856-1954), and 1966 ONS census.

Safi-Morocco.name: Safi
Safi-Morocco.evidence_basis: Atlantic grain port revitalized after 1930s by sardine canning and Youssoufia phosphate exports; Recensements du Maroc (1926-1952) and RGPH (1960: 81,072; 1971: 129,113).

Sidi Bel Abbes-Algeria.name: Sidi Bel Abbes
Sidi Bel Abbes-Algeria.evidence_basis: Founded 1843 as French Foreign Legion headquarters; Recensements Generaux de l'Algerie (1856-1954, high Spanish/French colon share) and 1966 ONS census showing slow 1954-1966 net change after 1962 exodus.

Tlemcen-Algeria.name: Tlemcen
Tlemcen-Algeria.evidence_basis: 1836 French military estimates of the historic Zayyanid capital (~14k), Recensements Generaux de l'Algerie (1856-1954 municipal counts), and 1966 ONS census.

Skikda-Algeria.name: Skikda
Skikda-Algeria.evidence_basis: Founded 1838 by Marshal Valee as Constantine's coastal port (Philippeville); Recensements Generaux de l'Algerie (1856-1954) and 1966 ONS census.

Batna-Algeria.name: Batna
Batna-Algeria.evidence_basis: Founded 1844 as French garrison guarding the Aures pass; Recensements Generaux de l'Algerie (1856-1954: ~18k-22k urban core) and 1966 ONS census (55,751) capturing massive wartime displacement from the Aures.

Bejaia-Algeria.name: Bejaia
Bejaia-Algeria.evidence_basis: 1833 French landing survey (~2.4k in declined medieval port), expanded by Petite Kabylie trade and 1959 Hassi Messaoud pipeline terminal; Recensements Generaux de l'Algerie (1856-1954) and 1966 ONS census.

Biskra-Algeria.name: Biskra
Biskra-Algeria.evidence_basis: Principal Ziban palm oasis occupied 1844 and linked by railway 1888; sole full-status Saharan commune in 1954 Recensement General (52,511 commune) and 1966 ONS census (59,275 urban core).

Mostaganem-Algeria.name: Mostaganem
Mostaganem-Algeria.evidence_basis: Pre-colonial Oranian port occupied 1833; Recensements Generaux de l'Algerie (1856-1954 municipal counts) and 1966 ONS census (60,218).

Khouribga-Morocco.name: Khouribga
Khouribga-Morocco.evidence_basis: OCP phosphate mining company town founded 1923 on the Ouled Abdoun plateau; Recensements du Maroc (1936-1952) and RGPH censuses (1960: 40,838; 1971: 73,667).

Chlef-Algeria.name: Chlef
Chlef-Algeria.evidence_basis: Founded 1843 by General Bugeaud on Roman Castellum Tingitanum (Orleansville); Recensements Generaux de l'Algerie (1856-1954; severely damaged by Sept 1954 earthquake) and 1966 ONS census.

Mohammedia-Morocco.name: Mohammedia
Mohammedia-Morocco.evidence_basis: Modern industrial and petroleum port founded 1913 (Fedala; renamed Mohammedia 1960 with SAMIR refinery); Recensements du Maroc (1936-1952) and RGPH (1960: 35,010; 1971: 70,392).

Sousse-Tunisia.name: Sousse
Sousse-Tunisia.evidence_basis: Principal Sahel port; 19th-c. consular estimates (~10k in 1830), Denombrements de la Tunisie (1921: 19,754; 1936: 28,465; 1946: 36,566), and INS censuses (1956: 48,172; 1975: 69,530).

Misrata-Libya.name: Misrata
Misrata-Libya.evidence_basis: Eastern Tripolitanian trade and carpet-weaving hub (urban core proper, excluding wider 1954 mutasarrifiyya of 66.7k); ISTAT colonial counts (1931-1936) and 1954/1964/1973 Libyan censuses.

Bizerte-Tunisia.name: Bizerte
Bizerte-Tunisia.evidence_basis: Transformed by 1895 French deep-water canal and naval base (damaged in 1942-43 WWII campaign); Denombrements de la Tunisie (1921-1946) and INS censuses (1956: 44,681; 1975: 62,856).

Medea-Algeria.name: Medea
Medea-Algeria.evidence_basis: Former capital of the Ottoman Beylik of Titteri (~7k in 1830); Recensements Generaux de l'Algerie (1856-1954 municipal counts) and 1966 ONS census.

Agadir-Morocco.name: Agadir
Agadir-Morocco.evidence_basis: Closed to foreign trade since 1765 (~1k in 1830-1912), boomed as fishing/Souss export port (1952: 30,111), devastated by 29 Feb 1960 earthquake (~15k killed; June 1960 RGPH: 16,695), rebuilt by 1971 (61,192).

Tebessa-Algeria.name: Tebessa
Tebessa-Algeria.evidence_basis: Walled Byzantine/Ottoman frontier town occupied 1851 and expanded by Kouif phosphate mining (1893); Recensements Generaux de l'Algerie (1856-1954) and 1966 ONS census.

El Jadida-Morocco.name: El Jadida
El Jadida-Morocco.evidence_basis: Rebuilt by Sultan Abd al-Rahman in 1824 as Doukkala grain export port (Mazagan); Recensements du Maroc (1926: 19,159; 1936: 24,391; 1952: 34,781) and RGPH (1960: 40,302; 1971: 55,501).

Taza-Morocco.name: Taza
Taza-Morocco.evidence_basis: Strategic corridor citadel between Fez and Oujda occupied 1914; Recensements du Maroc (1936: 14,973; 1952: 21,966) and RGPH censuses (1960: 31,667; 1971: 55,157).

Relizane-Algeria.name: Relizane
Relizane-Algeria.evidence_basis: Mina plain settlement expanded as French agricultural center (1857); exact Recensements Generaux de l'Algerie municipal counts (1936: 16,367; 1954: 27,772) and 1966 ONS census.

Guelma-Algeria.name: Guelma
Guelma-Algeria.evidence_basis: Small Seybouse valley settlement rebuilt as French garrison post in 1836; Recensements Generaux de l'Algerie (1856-1954 municipal counts) and 1966 ONS census.

Kairouan-Tunisia.name: Kairouan
Kairouan-Tunisia.evidence_basis: Inland religious and artisanal capital with slower growth than coastal ports; Denombrements de la Tunisie (1921: 19,401; 1936: 22,991; 1946: 32,299) and INS censuses (1956: 33,968; 1975: 54,546).

Bechar-Algeria.name: Bechar
Bechar-Algeria.evidence_basis: Founded 1903 as French frontier post Colomb-Bechar and expanded by Kenadsa coal mining (1917) and Mediterranean-Niger railway (1941); Territoires du Sud censuses (1954: ~14.8k) and 1966 ONS census.

Beni Mellal-Morocco.name: Beni Mellal
Beni Mellal-Morocco.evidence_basis: Tadla piedmont market town boosted by Bin el-Ouidane dam irrigation (1953); Recensements du Maroc (1936-1952) and RGPH censuses (1960: 28,933; 1971: 53,826).

Tiaret-Algeria.name: Tiaret
Tiaret-Algeria.evidence_basis: Re-established 1843 as French highland fort on Sersou cereal plateau; Recensements Generaux de l'Algerie (1856-1954) and 1966 ONS census.

Mascara-Algeria.name: Mascara
Mascara-Algeria.evidence_basis: Emir Abd al-Qadir's capital (~11.5k in 1830s, heavily depopulated after 1835/1841 French capture), Recensements Generaux de l'Algerie (1856-1954 commune counts), and 1966 ONS census (40,331).

Bordj Bou Arreridj-Algeria.name: Bordj Bou Arreridj
Bordj Bou Arreridj-Algeria.evidence_basis: Ottoman fort controlling the Bibans pass and Medjana plain (damaged in 1871 Mokrani revolt); Recensements Generaux de l'Algerie (1856-1954) and 1966 ONS census.

Souk Ahras-Algeria.name: Souk Ahras
Souk Ahras-Algeria.evidence_basis: Medjerda border market organized as French center 1852 and rail junction to Tunisia (1884); Recensements Generaux de l'Algerie (1856-1954) and 1966 ONS census.

Saida-Algeria.name: Saida
Saida-Algeria.evidence_basis: Abd al-Qadir fortress razed 1841 and rebuilt as French Foreign Legion post (1844) and esparto-grass railhead; Recensements Generaux de l'Algerie (1856-1954) and 1966 ONS census.

Zawiya-Libya.name: Zawiya
Zawiya-Libya.evidence_basis: Western Jefara coastal oasis center (town proper, distinct from 1954 agricultural district of 115k) boosted by 1970s refinery; ISTAT (1931-1936) and Libyan censuses (1954-1973).

Ksar el-Kebir-Morocco.name: Ksar el-Kebir
Ksar el-Kebir-Morocco.evidence_basis: Loukkos plain market city occupied by Spain 1911; Spanish Protectorate censuses (1936: 30,762; 1950: 35,786) and RGPH censuses (1960: 34,035; 1971: 48,262).

Ghardaia-Algeria.name: Ghardaia
Ghardaia-Algeria.evidence_basis: Primary ksar of the Ibadi Mzab pentapolis annexed 1882; Territoires du Sud enumerations (1954 urban core ~14k-15k within ~25k Mzab valley) and 1966 ONS census.

Larache-Morocco.name: Larache
Larache-Morocco.evidence_basis: Loukkos estuary port occupied by Spain 1911; Spanish Protectorate censuses (1936: 29,477; 1950: 41,898, including Spanish residents who departed after 1956) and RGPH (1960: 30,763; 1971: 45,710).

Khenchela-Algeria.name: Khenchela
Khenchela-Algeria.evidence_basis: Eastern Aures foothills garrison established 1850 on Roman Mascula; Recensements Generaux de l'Algerie (1856-1954) and 1966 ONS census.

Djelfa-Algeria.name: Djelfa
Djelfa-Algeria.evidence_basis: Steppe pastoral post organized by France 1852 and terminus of Blida narrow-gauge railway (1921); Recensements Generaux de l'Algerie (1954: ~10.5k) and 1966 ONS census (~26.1k) capturing Ouled Nail sedentarization.

Jijel-Algeria.name: Jijel
Jijel-Algeria.evidence_basis: Petite Kabylie coastal port occupied 1839 and rebuilt after 1856 earthquake; Recensements Generaux de l'Algerie (1856-1954) and 1966 ONS census.

El Oued-Algeria.name: El Oued
El Oued-Algeria.evidence_basis: Capital of the Souf sunken-garden palm oases occupied 1854; Territoires du Sud enumerations (1936-1954 urban core) and 1966 ONS census.

Bou Saada-Algeria.name: Bou Saada
Bou Saada-Algeria.evidence_basis: Northernmost Hodna desert oasis occupied 1849 and colonial winter resort; Recensements Generaux de l'Algerie (1856-1954) and 1966 ONS census.

Settat-Morocco.name: Settat
Settat-Morocco.evidence_basis: Historic Chaouia kasbah and grain market town occupied 1908; Recensements du Maroc (1936: 18,156; 1952: 25,205) and RGPH censuses (1960: 29,617; 1971: 42,325).

Tizi Ouzou-Algeria.name: Tizi Ouzou
Tizi Ouzou-Algeria.evidence_basis: Ottoman bordj expanded into French administrative seat of Grande Kabylie (1858); compact municipal core through 1954 (~5k-7k, excluding densely populated rural Kabyle douars) surging during wartime regroupement and post-1962 in 1966 ONS census.

Gafsa-Tunisia.name: Gafsa
Gafsa-Tunisia.evidence_basis: Southwest oasis boosted by 1897 Compagnie des Phosphates de Gafsa rail and mining boom; Denombrements de la Tunisie (1921-1946) and INS censuses (1956: 24,345; 1975: 42,225).

Ouargla-Algeria.name: Ouargla
Ouargla-Algeria.evidence_basis: Medieval caravan oasis occupied 1872 and named Oasis department capital in 1959 amid Saharan oil boom; Territoires du Sud censuses (1936-1954) and 1966 ONS census.

Menzel Bourguiba-Tunisia.name: Menzel Bourguiba
Menzel Bourguiba-Tunisia.evidence_basis: Founded 1897 as French naval arsenal town Ferryville on Lake Bizerte; Denombrements de la Tunisie (1921-1946) and INS censuses (1956: 34,732; plateauing in 1966 after 1963 French naval base evacuation).

Touggourt-Algeria.name: Touggourt
Touggourt-Algeria.evidence_basis: Historic Ben Djellab sultanate seat occupied 1854 and railhead from Biskra (1914); Territoires du Sud censuses (1936-1954) and 1966 ONS census.

Laghouat-Algeria.name: Laghouat
Laghouat-Algeria.evidence_basis: Saharan Atlas oasis (~4.2k before heavy 1852 French siege casualties), Territoires du Sud censuses (1936: ~7.9k; 1954: ~11.5k oasis town), and 1966 ONS census.

Gabes-Tunisia.name: Gabes
Gabes-Tunisia.evidence_basis: Maritime oasis hub of southern Tunisia; Denombrements de la Tunisie (1921-1946 municipal counts) and INS censuses (1956: 24,420; 1975: 40,585).

Beja-Tunisia.name: Beja
Beja-Tunisia.evidence_basis: Medjerda wheat-belt market town linked by rail in 1888; Denombrements de la Tunisie (1921-1946) and INS censuses (1956: 22,668; 1975: 39,226).

Boufarik-Algeria.name: Boufarik
Boufarik-Algeria.evidence_basis: Founded 1836 by Marshal Clauzel as prototype French settler town in drained Mitidja marshes; Recensements Generaux de l'Algerie (1856-1954) and 1966 ONS census.

M'Sila-Algeria.name: M'Sila
M'Sila-Algeria.evidence_basis: Historic Hodna basin town along the steppe border; Recensements Generaux de l'Algerie (1856-1954 urban core) and 1966 ONS census.

Ain Temouchent-Algeria.name: Ain Temouchent
Ain Temouchent-Algeria.evidence_basis: Founded 1851 as European viticultural colonization center on Roman Albulae; Recensements Generaux de l'Algerie (1856-1954; 1954: 25,187) and 1966 ONS census.

Tobruk-Libya.name: Tobruk
Tobruk-Libya.evidence_basis: Founded 1911 as Italian naval base on natural harbor (destroyed in 1941-42 WWII sieges, rebuilt and boosted by 1967 Marsa al-Hariga oil terminal); ISTAT (1931-1936) and Libyan censuses (1954 urban core: 4,995; 1964: 15,867).

Sabha-Libya.name: Sabha
Sabha-Libya.evidence_basis: Fezzan oasis elevated over Murzuq by Italian fort Elena (1930) and French military administration (1943-1951); 1954 UN/Libyan census (7,193) and 1964/1973 censuses.

Derna-Libya.name: Derna
Derna-Libya.evidence_basis: Andalusian-influenced Jabal Akhdar coastal port; ISTAT colonial censuses (1931-1936) and Libyan censuses (1954 urban core: 15,891; 1964: 21,432; 1973: 35,780).

Al-Bayda-Libya.name: Al-Bayda
Al-Bayda-Libya.evidence_basis: Founded c.1840 as Sanusi mother zawiya (depopulated during 1923-31 war, colonized as Beda Littoria, chosen as Kingdom of Libya administrative capital 1960s); ISTAT and 1954/1964/1973 Libyan censuses.

M'saken-Tunisia.name: M'saken
M'saken-Tunisia.evidence_basis: Large inland Sahel olive-growing agro-town; Denombrements de la Tunisie (1921-1946) and INS censuses (1956: 14,760; 1975: 33,559).

Bouira-Algeria.name: Bouira
Bouira-Algeria.evidence_basis: Turkish borj on Algiers-Constantine route turned colonial center in 1873; Recensements Generaux de l'Algerie (1856-1954) and 1966 ONS census.

Nador-Morocco.name: Nador
Nador-Morocco.evidence_basis: Eastern Rif lagoon post developed by Spain (1909) near Ouixan iron mines; Spanish Protectorate counts (1936-1950) and RGPH censuses (1960: 17,583; 1971: 32,490).

Ajdabiya-Libya.name: Ajdabiya
Ajdabiya-Libya.evidence_basis: Sanusi emirate seat (1917-1923) turned Sirte Basin oil-boom gateway after 1959 Zelten strike; ISTAT (1931-1936) and 1954/1964/1973 Libyan censuses.

Zliten-Libya.name: Zliten
Zliten-Libya.evidence_basis: Coastal Tripolitanian oasis and Islamic scholarly center (Al-Asmariya zawiya); urban town core in ISTAT (1931-1936) and 1954/1964/1973 Libyan censuses.

Nabeul-Tunisia.name: Nabeul
Nabeul-Tunisia.evidence_basis: Cap Bon pottery and citrus capital; Denombrements de la Tunisie (1921-1946) and INS censuses (1956: 11,990; 1966: 15,765; 1975: 30,476).

Essaouira-Morocco.name: Essaouira
Essaouira-Morocco.evidence_basis: Premier 19th-century Alawite international trade port (~13k-17k, Schroeter) that stagnated after Casablanca and Agadir eclipsed its harbor; Recensements du Maroc (1926-1952) and RGPH (1960: 26,392; 1971: 30,061).

Sefrou-Morocco.name: Sefrou
Sefrou-Morocco.evidence_basis: Middle Atlas piedmont walled town with major historic Jewish mellah (Rosen/Geertz studies); Recensements du Maroc (1936: 12,214; 1952: 16,590) and RGPH (1960: 21,478; 1971: 28,607).

El Bayadh-Algeria.name: El Bayadh
El Bayadh-Algeria.evidence_basis: Founded 1852 as French military fort Geryville controlling the western High Plateaux; Territoires du Sud censuses (1881-1954) and 1966 ONS census.

El Aaiun-Western Sahara.name: El Aaiun
El Aaiun-Western Sahara.evidence_basis: Founded 1938 by Captain Antonio de Oro as capital of Saguia el-Hamra; exact Spanish INE censuses (1950: 1,359; 1967: 16,319; 1970: 24,048; 1974: 28,010 excluding rotating garrison troops).

Le Kef-Tunisia.name: Le Kef
Le Kef-Tunisia.evidence_basis: Northwestern frontier garrison and grain-plateau administrative seat; Denombrements de la Tunisie (1921-1946) and INS censuses (1956: 14,416; 1975: 27,939).

Monastir-Tunisia.name: Monastir
Monastir-Tunisia.evidence_basis: Historic Sahel coastal town expanded post-1956 under President Bourguiba; Denombrements de la Tunisie (1921-1946) and INS censuses (1956: 13,594; 1975: 26,759).

Moknine-Tunisia.name: Moknine
Moknine-Tunisia.evidence_basis: Sahel artisan and olive-oil market town between Monastir and Mahdia; Denombrements de la Tunisie (1921-1946) and INS censuses (1956: 11,410; 1975: 26,035).

Mahdia-Tunisia.name: Mahdia
Mahdia-Tunisia.evidence_basis: Sahel fishing and olive port on former Fatimid peninsula; Denombrements de la Tunisie (1921-1946) and INS censuses (1956: 12,795; 1975: 25,711).

Al-Khums-Libya.name: Al-Khums
Al-Khums-Libya.evidence_basis: Ottoman esparto-grass port near Leptis Magna (1880s-1911); ISTAT urban counts (1931-1936) and 1954/1964/1973 Libyan censuses (town proper, excluding rural Cussabat district).

Arzew-Algeria.name: Arzew
Arzew-Algeria.evidence_basis: Modern port founded 1845 near Roman Portus Magnus, expanded rapidly after 1964 LNG liquefaction terminal opening; Recensements Generaux de l'Algerie (1856-1954) and 1966 ONS census.

Zuwara-Libya.name: Zuwara
Zuwara-Libya.evidence_basis: Amazigh coastal fishing and salt-pan town near Tunisian border (occupied 1912); ISTAT (1931-1936) and 1954/1964/1973 Libyan censuses (town proper).

Cherchell-Algeria.name: Cherchell
Cherchell-Algeria.evidence_basis: Andalusian coastal town occupied 1840 (later site of military academy); Recensements Generaux de l'Algerie (1856-1954) and 1966 ONS census.

Al-Marj-Libya.name: Al-Marj
Al-Marj-Libya.evidence_basis: Jabal Akhdar plateau town expanded as Italian Ente Colonizzazione agricultural center (Barce; devastated by Feb 1963 earthquake and relocated); ISTAT (1931-1936) and 1954/1964/1973 Libyan censuses.

Kasserine-Tunisia.name: Kasserine
Kasserine-Tunisia.evidence_basis: High-steppe pass town (site of 1943 WWII battle) elevated to governorate capital in 1956 with alfa-pulp mill (1963); Denombrements de la Tunisie and INS censuses (1956-1975).

Taroudant-Morocco.name: Taroudant
Taroudant-Morocco.evidence_basis: Walled Souss Valley capital with remarkably stable pre-1940 population (~8k-8.6k); Recensements du Maroc (1936: 8,596; 1952: 12,877) and RGPH (1960: 17,141; 1971: 22,272).

Ain Sefra-Algeria.name: Ain Sefra
Ain Sefra-Algeria.evidence_basis: Ksour oasis fortified by France 1881 and linked by rail 1887 (Territoires du Sud headquarters of Ain Sefra); colonial censuses (1881-1954) and 1966 ONS census.

Sabratha-Libya.name: Sabratha
Sabratha-Libya.evidence_basis: Western Tripolitanian coastal oasis adjacent to Roman Sabratha excavated in the 1920s-1930s; ISTAT counts and 1954/1964/1973 Libyan censuses.

Gharyan-Libya.name: Gharyan
Gharyan-Libya.evidence_basis: Principal Nafusa highland market center (compact town core distinct from wider Jabal al-Gharbi tribal district); ISTAT (1931-1936) and 1954/1964/1973 Libyan censuses.

Al Hoceima-Morocco.name: Al Hoceima
Al Hoceima-Morocco.evidence_basis: Founded 1926 as Spanish garrison port Villa Sanjurjo following the Rif War landing; Spanish zone census (1950: 10,770) and RGPH censuses (1960: 11,262; 1971: 18,686).

Jendouba-Tunisia.name: Jendouba
Jendouba-Tunisia.evidence_basis: Upper Medjerda cereal rail town (Souk El Arba, Tunis-Algiers line 1880); Denombrements de la Tunisie (1921-1946) and INS censuses (1956-1975).

Tenes-Algeria.name: Tenes
Tenes-Algeria.evidence_basis: Historic Dahra port occupied 1843 as supply outlet for Orleansville; Recensements Generaux de l'Algerie (1856-1954) and 1966 ONS census.

Tarhuna-Libya.name: Tarhuna
Tarhuna-Libya.evidence_basis: Inland Gefara plateau agricultural center (nucleated town proper distinct from wider tribal district); ISTAT (1931-1936) and 1954/1964/1973 Libyan censuses.

Errachidia-Morocco.name: Errachidia
Errachidia-Morocco.evidence_basis: Ziz Valley ksar turned French Tafilalt military headquarters (Ksar es-Souk, 1916); Protectorate counts (1936-1952) and RGPH censuses (1960-1971).

Tozeur-Tunisia.name: Tozeur
Tozeur-Tunisia.evidence_basis: Principal Djerid date-palm oasis linked to Gafsa-Sfax railway in 1913; Denombrements de la Tunisie (1921-1946) and INS censuses (1956-1975).

Hammamet-Tunisia.name: Hammamet
Hammamet-Tunisia.evidence_basis: Walled Cap Bon fishing and citrus town developing tourism in the 1960s; Denombrements de la Tunisie (1921-1946) and INS censuses (1956: 9,522; 1975: 16,505).

Sirte-Libya.name: Sirte
Sirte-Libya.evidence_basis: Small Ottoman fortress town (Qasr Zafran, 1842) along Via Balbia (1937) linking Tripolitania and Cyrenaica; ISTAT and 1954/1964/1973 Libyan censuses.

Medenine-Tunisia.name: Medenine
Medenine-Tunisia.evidence_basis: Ksar granary complex turned French Southern Military Territories headquarters (1882); Denombrements de la Tunisie (1921-1946) and INS censuses (1956-1975).

Chefchaouen-Morocco.name: Chefchaouen
Chefchaouen-Morocco.evidence_basis: Rif mountain town occupied by Spain 1920/1926; Spanish Protectorate censuses (1936-1950: 13,712) and RGPH censuses (1960-1971).

Guelmim-Morocco.name: Guelmim
Guelmim-Morocco.evidence_basis: Oued Noun trans-Saharan caravan market (Beyruk trading house); French military post (1934) and RGPH censuses (1960-1971).

Midelt-Morocco.name: Midelt
Midelt-Morocco.evidence_basis: Founded 1917 as French administrative center for Aouli and Mibladen lead mines; exact 1936 Protectorate record (1,719 residents) and 1960/1971 RGPH censuses.

Souk et Tnine Jorf el Mellah-Morocco.name: Souk et Tnine Jorf el Mellah

El Golea-Algeria.name: El Golea
El Golea-Algeria.evidence_basis: Central Saharan artesian oasis occupied 1873 and developed as trans-Saharan waystation; Territoires du Sud censuses (1911-1954) and 1966 ONS census.

Dellys-Algeria.name: Dellys
Dellys-Algeria.evidence_basis: Small Ottoman coastal town occupied 1844, seat of colonial Ecole d'Arts et Metiers; Recensements Generaux de l'Algerie (1856-1954) and 1966 ONS census.

Zarzis-Tunisia.name: Zarzis
Zarzis-Tunisia.evidence_basis: Southeastern sponge-fishing and olive coastal oasis near Tripolitanian border; Denombrements de la Tunisie (1921-1946) and INS censuses (1956-1975).

Adrar-Algeria.name: Adrar
Adrar-Algeria.evidence_basis: Touat oasis ksour cluster occupied by France in 1900; Territoires du Sud military censuses (1911-1954) and 1966 ONS census.

Sidi Ifni-Morocco.name: Sidi Ifni
Sidi Ifni-Morocco.evidence_basis: Founded 1934 as capital of Spanish Ifni enclave (retroceded to Morocco 1969); Spanish INE censuses (1950: 7,991; 1960: 12,751) and 1971 RGPH census.

Hassi Messaoud-Algeria.name: Hassi Messaoud
Hassi Messaoud-Algeria.evidence_basis: Founded 1956 as Saharan petroleum camp following SN Repal/CFP-A oil strike; zero permanent urban population prior to 1956; 1966 ONS census and 1975 hydrocarbon workforce growth.

Tamanrasset-Algeria.name: Tamanrasset
Tamanrasset-Algeria.evidence_basis: Ahaggar Tuareg cultivation hamlet fortified as Fort-Laperrine (1920); Territoires du Sud post counts (1936-1954) and 1966 ONS census before trans-Saharan highway growth.

Timimoun-Algeria.name: Timimoun
Timimoun-Algeria.evidence_basis: Chief ksar of the Gourara foggara oases occupied 1900; Territoires du Sud censuses (1911-1954) and 1966 ONS census.

Tiznit-Morocco.name: Tiznit
Tiznit-Morocco.evidence_basis: Walled Anti-Atlas garrison town rebuilt by Sultan Hassan I in 1881-1882; Recensements du Maroc (1936-1952: 6,476) and RGPH censuses (1960: 7,694; 1971: 11,391).

Ouarzazate-Morocco.name: Ouarzazate
Ouarzazate-Morocco.evidence_basis: Founded 1928 as French garrison and regional administrative post adjacent to Glaoui Taourirt kasbah; Protectorate counts (1936-1952) and RGPH censuses (1960-1971).

In Salah-Algeria.name: In Salah
In Salah-Algeria.evidence_basis: Tidikelt caravan hub occupied by Flamand-Pein mission in Dec 1899; Territoires du Sud enumerations (1911-1954) and 1966 ONS census.

Hun-Libya.name: Hun
Hun-Libya.evidence_basis: Capital of Al-Jufra oasis group and headquarters of Italian Territorio Militare del Sud (1934-1943); ISTAT colonial records and 1954/1964/1973 Libyan censuses.

Nalut-Libya.name: Nalut
Nalut-Libya.evidence_basis: Western Nafusa Berber mountain town and fortified granary (Ksar Nalut) on the Tunisian border; ISTAT (1931-1936) and 1954/1964/1973 Libyan censuses.

Tataouine-Tunisia.name: Tataouine
Tataouine-Tunisia.evidence_basis: Far-southern Berber ksour market and French Bat' d'Af disciplinary garrison (1892); Denombrements de la Tunisie (1921-1946) and INS censuses (1956-1975).

Al-Jawf-Libya.name: Al-Jawf
Al-Jawf-Libya.evidence_basis: Chief oasis of Kufra archipelago and Sanusi order headquarters (1895-1931; severe depopulation during 1931 Italian conquest); ISTAT (1931-1936) and 1954/1964/1973 Libyan censuses.

Murzuq-Libya.name: Murzuq
Murzuq-Libya.evidence_basis: Historic Ottoman Fezzan capital and trans-Saharan slave/caravan emporium (~3.5k in 1830s, Lyon/Barth/Nachtigal) that declined as Saharan trade waned and Sabha took administrative primacy; ISTAT and 1954/1964/1973 censuses.

Smara-Western Sahara.name: Smara
Smara-Western Sahara.evidence_basis: Founded 1898 by Shaykh Ma al-Aynayn, sacked by French Mouret column in 1913, occupied by Spain 1934; exact 1967 INE census (2,130) and 1974 census surge (7,280) driven by drought sedentarization.

Tindouf-Algeria.name: Tindouf
Tindouf-Algeria.evidence_basis: Tajakant oasis town founded 1852 (sacked by Reguibat 1895, occupied by France 1934); Territoires du Sud counts (1936-1954) and 1966 ONS census (excluding post-1975 Sahrawi refugee camps).

Ghadames-Libya.name: Ghadames
Ghadames-Libya.evidence_basis: Famed trans-Saharan merchant oasis (~4k in 1830s-1860s, Richardson/Mircher) declining with caravan trade collapse until 1950s recovery; ISTAT (1936: ~3,020) and 1954/1964/1973 Libyan censuses.

Dakhla-Western Sahara.name: Dakhla
Dakhla-Western Sahara.evidence_basis: Founded 1884 by Emilio Bonelli as Spanish Rio de Oro factory and capital until 1940; exact Spanish INE censuses (1950: ~1.1k; 1967: 5,454; 1970: 5,570; 1974: 5,370).

Ghat-Libya.name: Ghat
Ghat-Libya.evidence_basis: Kel Ajjer Tuareg caravan oasis (~2k in 19th c., Barth/Duveyrier) occupied by Italy 1930 and France 1943-1951; ISTAT and 1954/1964/1973 Libyan censuses.

Souk El Arba Des Ait Baha-Morocco.name: Souk El Arba Des Ait Baha

Bou Craa-Western Sahara.name: Bou Craa
Bou Craa-Western Sahara.evidence_basis: ENMINSA/Fosbucraa phosphate mining company town developed from 1963 with commercial extraction beginning 1972; 1974 Spanish Sahara census industrial workforce count.

Tarfaya-Morocco.name: Tarfaya
Tarfaya-Morocco.evidence_basis: Founded 1879 as British Port Victoria trading factory, occupied by Spain 1916 as Villa Bens (capital of Spanish Southern Protectorate until 1958); Spanish colonial counts (1950) and 1960/1971 RGPH.

Guelta Zemmur-Western Sahara.name: Guelta Zemmur
Guelta Zemmur-Western Sahara.evidence_basis: Permanent Saharan waterhole established as Spanish interior military and tribal assembly post in 1934; Spanish Sahara district records (1967-1974).

Ausserd-Western Sahara.name: Ausserd
Ausserd-Western Sahara.evidence_basis: Southern Rio de Oro interior post established 1934 as Spanish nomadic administration center; Spanish Sahara district records (1967-1974).

Boujdour-Western Sahara.name: Boujdour
Boujdour-Western Sahara.evidence_basis: Coastal lighthouse post organized as permanent fishing and administrative settlement only at the very end of Spanish rule in 1975 (~1.2k).
